A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 18-page versions of the same LoR-VP paper, including Appendices A and B. Text and visual comparison establish that differences are confined to pages 1 and 7; all other pages render identically.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, robustness, efficiency and ablation experiments in Sections 3 and 5, plus detection, segmentation and additional classification results in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the main experimental figures and Appendix B's detection, segmentation and classification results in Tables 9–12.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same additive low-rank prompt, matrix initialization, optimization objective and linear-probing output transformation. Equations 1–2 and the method components are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same classification and ImageNet distribution-shift datasets. Appendix B's ten-dataset classification suite and Pascal VOC detection and segmentation tasks are already present in v1 and remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments. Figure 4 retains CLIP-VP, ILM-VP, AutoVP and LP; Table 11 retains VPT alongside the other baselines; Tables 9–10 retain LP and AutoVP.

E3.justification: The versions report identical preprocessing, model configurations, splits, metrics and training budgets. This includes the classification settings in Section 5.1 and Table 8 and the detection and segmentation protocols in Appendix B.

E4.justification: The preliminary prompt-design comparison, distribution-shift evaluation, rank sensitivity and component/output-transformation ablations are unchanged. Appendix B's additional LP-versus-FM analysis and Table 12 are retained without revision.

E5.justification: Figures 2, 4 and 5 retain the statement that results are averaged over three runs. Run-count information and uncertainty reporting remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices.

E6.justification: All matched numerical results, curves and findings are unchanged, with no result entries added or removed. Examples include LoR-VP's 84.04 ImageNet-1K accuracy in Table 1, 77.02 VOC detection AP50 in Table 9 and 88.94 average accuracy in Table 11.

T1.justification: The mathematical setup in Section 3.1 and prompt and optimization definitions in Equations 1–2 are identical. No assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and efficiency/performance claims, including shared and patch-specific prompting, up to sixfold faster training, eighteenfold fewer prompt parameters and a 3.1% performance improvement.

C2.justification: Explanations concerning image continuity, shared prompting, output-mapping scalability and rank selection are unchanged. Both retain the computational constraints discussed in Section 5.2 and Appendix B's interpretation of AutoVP's dataset-dependent scaling effects.

D1.justification: The embedded code hyperlink changes from a destination ending in 'LoR-VP.' to 'LoR-VP', removing sentence punctuation from the repository path. The disclosed repository, model-source URLs, hardware, hyperparameters and appendix implementation details otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the bibliography and the paper's positioning relative to earlier visual prompting and low-rank adaptation work are unchanged. No cited works or novelty relationships are added or removed.

P1.justification: v3 corrects NVIDIA Research's affiliation marker from 3 to 5, changes 'Code is available as' to 'Code is available at', and reformats the correspondence line. Section order, terminology and substantive prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Footnote and correspondence formatting changes produce slight local reflow on pages 1 and 7. Numbered footnote markers and the email's embedded hyperlink are removed. Figure and table designs remain unchanged, and all other pages render identically.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects the author-affiliation numbering and removes stray punctuation from the code hyperlink's destination, providing small gains in attribution accuracy and access usability. The email loses its embedded hyperlink but remains printed. Scientific content and appendix evidence are unchanged, so the overall improvement is limited.
